name: Cross-sectional laggard reversion — long the worst relative performers (short-horizon)
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM (the OPPOSITE-SIGN read of xsec_momentum_rank vs every existing xsec spec: xsec-neutral-momentum-long-leg and cross-asset-social-rotation go long the HIGH-rank LEADERS; this goes long the LOW-rank LAGGARDS): at the cross-sectional level, momentum dominates at the medium horizon (weeks-to-months) but REVERSAL dominates at the SHORT horizon (days) — the documented short-term cross-sectional reversal (Lehmann 1990, Lo-MacKinlay): the week's biggest relative losers over-shoot on the downside and snap back as liquidity providers are compensated for absorbing the selling. So ranking by the SHORT-window relative return and buying the BOTTOM of the cross-section (low rank) harvests the reversal premium that is orthogonal to (and opposite in horizon from) the medium-term momentum the existing xsec leaders capture. The rank is computed point-in-time over instruments present at the bar (no survivorship). To avoid catching a structurally broken name, gate on a non-collapsing realized vol (sit out turbulent regimes) and exit when the laggard has mean-reverted back up the cross-section. Entry: xsec_momentum_rank below a fitted low-rank floor (a relative laggard) over a SHORT lookback AND vol_realized below a fitted ceiling (calm enough for reversion). Exit: xsec_momentum_rank crosses UP through a mid-rank threshold (reverted) or stop/TP/time. Disconfirmer 1: if buying low-rank does NO better than a coin-flip after costs, short-term reversal has no exploitable edge net of ~20bps. Disconfirmer 2: this is the directional inverse of the momentum-rank leaders — the two must NOT be double-counted (same feature, opposite tail, different horizon). Disconfirmer 3 (HORIZON is the thesis): if a MEDIUM lookback works as well, the short-horizon reversal claim is unsupported and this collapses into anti-momentum noise. Disconfirmer 4: low rank can mean a dying asset — the vol gate and PIT universe must guard survivorship. tier0 cohort-computed feature.
catalyst: the short-horizon cross-sectional losers over-shoot and mean-revert up
